summary: A solicitation from SRI-ARC asking whether network users wanted on-site classes on NLS, the oNLine System, rather than traveling to SRI. It outlines course contents and logistics, and tentatively proposes trips to Washington D.C. in early May and Boston in early June.

plainLanguage.summary: The people who made a program offered to visit other places to teach it, and asked if anyone wanted lessons.

subtitle: SRI-ARC offers to visit network sites and teach the Online System.

tldr.problem: Network users wanted to learn NLS (the Online System), a powerful tool developed at SRI-ARC, but training required traveling to California.
tldr.mechanism: SRI-ARC offered to conduct on-site classes at network sites instead, covering basic and advanced NLS features with customized agendas for different needs.
tldr.outcome: The RFC solicits responses from network sites to determine interest in hosting classes, tentatively proposing visits to Washington D.C. in May and Boston in June.

facts.label: Training completed by March 1973
facts.value: About a dozen classes, nearly 100 people

today: RFC 488 is a historical announcement of training offered in 1973. NLS evolved into modern hypertext systems like the web.

sections.title: Training NLS Remotely
sections.content: RFC 488 announces that SRI-ARC, which created the Online System (NLS), would conduct training classes at network sites rather than only at SRI. The RFC describes a comprehensive two- to three-day course covering basic file manipulation, text handling, data structures, viewing options, searching and sorting. The class size is optimized for six to ten students, with one instructor leading and one or more assistants.
sections.plainLanguage: A program team wanted to teach their tool to people at other locations instead of making everyone come to them.

sections.title: Course Organization
sections.content: The class outline consists of three parts: Elementary Concepts (basic NLS commands and text editing), Entering and Using Information (data structures, file management, network features like LOCATOR and NIC/QUERY), and Sorting and Searching (sort, merge, and content analysis). The RFC emphasizes that the outline is flexible and can be tailored to address the specific interests and use cases at each site.
sections.plainLanguage: The lessons were split into three sections, from easy basics up to advanced tricks, and could change based on what people needed.

sections.title: Logistics and Response
sections.content: Sites interested in hosting a class needed to provide a classroom, teletype terminals for each student, a flip chart, and a blackboard. SRI-ARC requested responses by April 15, 1973, and proposed tentative visits to Washington D.C. in early May and Boston in early June, but said they would consider other arrangements. About a dozen NLS classes had been held at SRI-ARC by this time, training nearly a hundred people.
sections.plainLanguage: The instructors needed a room with computers for students, and asked sites to let them know if they wanted a visit.
